'''Armon Deshawn Johnson''' (born February 23, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played two seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played college basketball for [[Nevada Wolfpack men's basketball|Nevada]].

==College career==
In his three-year career at [[Nevada Wolfpack men's basketball|Nevada]], Johnson averaged 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 4.4 assists in 101 games.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/armon-johnson-1.html Armon Johnson Stats]</ref>

==Professional career==
Johnson was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the 34th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. On August 2, 2010, he signed with the Trail Blazers after averaging 11.6 points and 4.2 assists in five summer league games.<ref>[https://blog.oregonlive.com/blazers/2010/08/trail_blazers_sign_rookie_guar.html Trail Blazers sign rookie guard Armon Johnson]</ref> After a promising debut game on October 26, 2010, in which he scored six points with two rebounds and three assists in nine minutes, Johnson went on to have three double-figure scoring games in November, reaching a high in playing time of 22 minutes. However, his minutes and production declined over the following two months.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/johnsar02/gamelog/2011 Basketball Reference]</ref>

On January 28, 2011, he was assigned to the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kolotv.com/home/headlines/114820769.html |title=Former Pack Standout, Hug Grad Johnson Assigned To D-League |access-date=2011-01-29 |archive-date=2013-01-27 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130127091554/http://www.kolotv.com/home/headlines/114820769.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was recalled on February 22, 2011, then reassigned on January 4, 2012, and recalled again on January 15, 2012. On February 27, 2012, he was waived by the Trail Blazers. He signed a ten-day contract with the [[New Jersey Nets]] on April 9, 2012.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Armon_10day_Release_120409.html Nets Sign Armon Johnson to 10-Day Contract]</ref> On April 20, he signed with the Nets for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Armon_Signing_Release_120420.html NETS Sign Armon Johnson for Remainder of Season]</ref>

On September 29, 2012, Johnson signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-johnson-jones-prepare-camp Magic Sign Johnson, Jones; Prepare for Camp]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Magic on October 23, 2012, after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-eyenga-johnson Magic Waive Eyenga, A. Johnson]</ref> In December 2012, he joined Kazakh powerhouse team [[BC Astana]].<ref>[https://www.asia-basket.com/Kazakhstan/basketball.aspx?NewsID=298609 Armon Johnson joins BC Astana]</ref> After scoring 13 points in his debut for Astana on December 16, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with a serious knee injury.<ref>[https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/college/nevada/2014/05/30/a-look-at-what-ex-wolf-pack-hug-star-armon-johnson-is-up-to/9769483/ A look at what ex-Wolf Pack/Hug star Armon Johnson is up to]</ref>

In March 2014, after passing a tryout period, Johnson signed with the Spanish team [[CB Valladolid]] for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=102444 Armon Johnson continuará en el CB Valladolid hasta final de temporada] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

On July 7, 2014, Johnson joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-2014-nba-summer-league-roster CLIPPERS ANNOUNCE 2014 NBA SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER]</ref> On July 29, he signed with [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket]] of France for the 2014–15 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/129430/le-mans-signs-armon-johnson.html Le Mans signs Armon Johnson]</ref> On October 29, 2014, he was waived by Le Mans after appearing in just five games.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/139367/le-mans-extends-daniel-ewing-for-the-season-waives-armon-johnson.html Le Mans extends Daniel Ewing for the season, waives Armon Johnson]</ref> On April 2, 2015, he was acquired by the [[Austin Spurs]] of the NBA Development League.<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4946044 Austin Spurs Acquire Armon Johnson]</ref>

On August 14, 2015, Johnson signed with [[BG Göttingen|Göttingen]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Armon Johnson moves to BG Goettingen|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/172764/armon-johnson-moves-to-bg-goettingen.html|accessdate=August 14, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 14, 2015}}</ref> On September 15, 2015, he parted ways with Göttingen before the start of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/175923/armon-johnson-bg-goettingen-part-ways.html Armon Johnson, BG Goettingen part ways]</ref>

In 2016, he joined the [[Nevada Senators ABA]] team in [[Reno, Nevada]].

==Coaching career==
Following his professional career, Johnson returned to the [[University of Nevada, Reno]] as an undergrad assistant under Head Coach [[Eric Musselman]]. After a couple year stint with the Wolf Pack, he was hired as the head coach of [[Excel Christian School]], a small 1A academy in [[Sparks, Nevada]].<ref>[https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/ex-wolf-pack-star-armon-johnson-named-excel-christians-head-coach Armon Johnson Named Excel Christian's Head Coach]</ref> In his one season at [[Excel Christian School]], Johnson failed to win a game, going 0–12.<ref>[https://www.maxpreps.com/high-schools/excel-christian-warriors-(sparks,nv)/basketball-19-20/schedule.htm 19–20 Excel Christian Varsity Basketball]</ref> In May 2021, Johnson was hired as the head varsity basketball coach for [[Robert McQueen High School]] where he currently coaches.<ref>[https://apnews.com/article/reno-sports-d3b444279763f06fd9b24b0a53f3c3c0 Ex-UNR star Armon Johnson new coach at Reno’s McQueen High]</ref> As of December 31, 2021, Johnson is 7–2 with the Lancers. His overall prep coaching record stands at 7–14.
